title: Scaling
summary: Convert raw values into engineering units with a straight-line formula and avoid integer traps.

sections.heading: Two points define a line
sections.body: Scaling maps the raw range onto the engineering range: `value = (raw - rawMin) / (rawMax - rawMin) * (engMax - engMin) + engMin`. Convert to REAL first to keep decimals.

sections.heading: The line
sections.body: Raw on the x axis, engineering value on the y axis.

sections.heading: Common mistake
sections.body: `LevelRaw / 10000 * 100` in INT arithmetic is 0 for every raw value below 10000, because the division truncates first.

question.question: LevelRaw = 5000. What is LevelRaw / 10000 * 100 in INT arithmetic?

sections.heading: Practice: fill to a setpoint
sections.body: Scale LevelRaw and stop filling at 60 %.

sections.heading: Summary and troubleshooting note
sections.body:
Scale with REAL arithmetic from two known points; know the raw range of your platform.

**Troubleshooting note:** When the scaled value is wrong only near zero, suspect the measuring range (0-20 vs 4-20 mA); when it is wrong everywhere, suspect the formula or the raw range.
